key_insight: An AI-assisted evaluation pipeline judges research-level mathematical proofs across multiple formats while reducing false-positive verdicts compared with one-shot LLM judgment.
engineering_relevance: The pipeline offers a methodology for evaluating complex mathematical submissions spanning natural language, computer algebra code, and Lean formalizations.
method: Analyze Ramanujan Challenge submissions on research-level number theory problems.
Assess semantic and logical correctness across natural language proofs, CAS code, and Lean formalizations.
Compare pipeline judgments with conventional one-shot LLM judgments.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports false-positive verdicts on natural language proofs falling from 23% to 6% and supporting-code judgment accuracy rising from 46% to 58%.
watch_item: Residual evaluation errors remain substantial, and the abstract does not specify sample sizes or generalization beyond this benchmark.
paper_title: Ramanujan Challenge Results: AI-Assisted Evaluation Pipeline for Multi-Format Proofs
